title: Zero Trust & Cloud Security
subtitle: Plan a zero trust adoption and protect data and AI systems in the cloud
audience_line: Security managers, architects and IT leaders planning a security strategy
overview: This workshop helps security and IT leaders plan a move to zero trust and protect data in the cloud. Participants learn the principles of NIST SP 800-207 and the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, with identity at the centre, then work on cloud data security: encryption and key management, data loss prevention and data residency. They see how AI changes detection and response and how to secure AI systems themselves. The workshop closes with a final project in which each team builds a zero trust adoption roadmap for a given organisation.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Security managers, architects and IT leaders planning a security strategy

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: None. A general IT or security background is expected (course: Cybersecurity for IT Teams, recommended)

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 15 h: 12 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Workshop: short lectures, each followed by group exercises on an organisation case

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant with a browser; maturity assessment templates; trainer demonstrations in the AWS console (KMS, Macie); no account or cost for participants

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: An exercise validated at the end of each phase and a final roadmap presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can assess an organisation against the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model and build a prioritised roadmap covering identity, data and AI systems

phases.name: Zero Trust
phases.focus: NIST SP 800-207, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, identity-centric security
phases.intro: Participants learn what zero trust means in practice: the tenets and architecture of NIST SP 800-207, the five pillars, three cross-cutting capabilities and four maturity stages of CISA ZTMM v2.0, and why identity becomes the main control. Validated exercise: the case organisation rated on the five CISA pillars.

chapters.title: Zero Trust Principles
chapters.content: NIST SP 800-207, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, identity-centric security

phases.name: Cloud Data & AI Security
phases.focus: Encryption and keys, DLP, data residency, AI for detection, securing AI systems
phases.intro: Participants decide how cloud data is encrypted and who holds the keys, where data loss prevention fits and how residency rules constrain the design, then look at AI on both sides: as a help for detection and response, and as a new system to secure. Validated exercise: a data protection plan for the case organisation's most sensitive data set.

chapters.title: Cloud Data Security
chapters.content: Encryption, key management, DLP, data residency

chapters.title: AI in Security
chapters.content: AI-enabled detection and response, securing AI systems

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A zero trust adoption roadmap, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three build a zero trust adoption roadmap for a given organisation, reusing the workshop exercises, and present it as they would to an executive committee.

chapters.title: Assess & Plan
chapters.content: Current maturity, target state, prioritised initiatives and milestones

chapters.title: Present & Review
chapters.content: Present the roadmap; questions and feedback

project.title: Zero Trust Adoption Roadmap
project.brief: A zero trust roadmap for a given organisation: current maturity on the CISA pillars, target state, prioritised initiatives for identity, data and AI systems, and milestones.
project.stack: NIST SP 800-207, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, assessment templates
